gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured figure for the Anker Nano Power Bank 10K 45W it recommended as 'premium choice': Gigazine measured it delivering only 34-36 W (never the rated 45 W) to a Pixel 10 Pro XL, spending 70% of the bank on one 5,200 mAh phone charge, and taking 160 minutes to recharge at a measured 29 W input.
standout_why: Compared against Engadget (Amy Skorheim, 2026-02-13: hands-on charge counts for Anker MagGo 10K and 10K Fusion, and a generic finding that 10,000 mAh banks delivered about 5,800 mAh), PowerBankOnline (admits it tested nothing; Amazon specs only), knowledgelib.io (unattributed snippets), Oscarmini (maker claims only), Anker's blog (maker claims). None of them measures any of the three banks ChatGPT actually recommended. TechRadar and WSJ could not be opened. Engadget's generic ~58% delivered-capacity figure means the 'real capacity is lower' idea is partly covered, so this is new and useful rather than pick-deciding.
decides: Confirms the Anker Nano 10K 45W as a credible pick for a phone (52% into an iPhone 15 in 30 minutes per Macworld; roughly 1.4 full charges of a 5,200 mAh Pixel implied by Gigazine's 70%-per-charge reading) but shows the 45 W headline is not reached with a phone, so a shopper buying for a phone alone gains little from the 45 W tier over a 30 W bank; the 2h15-2h40 recharge time is the concrete number no rival page gives. Also flags that the 'everyday choice' Anker 10K 22.5W is model A1257, which Oscarmini lists among Anker's June 2025 recall (certain serials).
